title: The Life and Work of Sid Grossman

description.main: The first comprehensive survey of the photographer Sid Grossman (1915-1955), edited with an essay by Keith F. Davis. Steidl with the Howard Greenberg Library, 2016.
description.extended:
The first comprehensive survey of the photographer and Photo League teacher Sid Grossman (1915–1955), edited and written by the curator Keith F. Davis.

Grossman was largely forgotten after his death and had been labeled a communist and blacklisted in 1949. The book reproduces more than 150 photographs. They run from social documentary work of the late 1930s to street photography of the late 1940s, then later experiments with abstraction in black and white and color. Davis's essay traces Grossman's development and his influence as a teacher. The book closes with excerpts from recordings of a course Grossman taught in the spring of 1950. Howard Greenberg wrote the foreword; Steidl published it with the Howard Greenberg Library.

Grossman was a founder of the Photo League (1936–51) in New York. Davis, senior curator of photography at the Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art, has also written on Dave Heath, Ray K. Metzker and Emmet Gowin.
